idempotency_key.name: Idempotency-Key
idempotency_key.description: The operation's key. A new operation takes a new key, and the same call sent again (after a network failure, or when no answer came back) takes the same key: the same key again answers what the first answered, and changes nothing. A submit or a resubmit made again with other values, or after a refusal, is a new operation, and takes a new key. Up to 255 bytes of visible ASCII (`!` to `~`, no space); another key is answered 400

limit.name: limit
limit.description: The most tickets the page holds; 50 when it is left out

q.name: q
q.description: The words to find by, apart with white space: up to 200 characters. None find every one

find_limit.name: limit
find_limit.description: The most it answers; 20 when it is left out

lang.name: lang
lang.description: The language of the names: `en` or `ja`; when it is left out, the first of them `Accept-Language` names, else `en`

before.name: before
before.description: The ID of the last ticket of the page before: the page holds the tickets after it in the list's order. Left out for the first page; a ticket the list does not hold gives an empty page

moved.description: The event is taken: the ticket as it is now

refused.description: The event is refused, and the ticket is as it was

unread.description: The request does not read, and the ticket is as it was: a body not of its shape (a value of another JSON type, a key it requires missing, a key it does not take, a day not written `YYYY-MM-DD`, a whole number past 64 bits, a revision with a key left out or outside its ranges), no idempotency key, one not of its form or one used before for another operation, a file it names that is neither one the ticket holds nor one the person uploaded (`no such file`), or a value the generated entry stops at as no input of the contract. What the person writes is the machine's to refuse (409) whatever the schemas say of it: as `form`, a value of the form or of a row it does not take (a choice not among its choices, a number outside its range, a text too long, too many rows, a field it asks for left empty, null or left out); as `comment`, a comment's text left empty or longer than 2,000 characters

unworked.description: The request does not read: a body not of its shape (a value of another JSON type, `form` left out or not an object, a key it does not take, a day not written `YYYY-MM-DD`, a whole number past 64 bits), or a value the generated entry `worked` stops at as no input of the contract, its error in the language of the list of kinds (`lang`). A value outside its field's range or none of its choices, and rows past the most their field takes, are no error: what reads them is answered as not decided (null); rows fewer than the field asks for are worked out as they are there

unasked.description: The read is not asked as it takes: of a list, a `limit` that is not a whole number from 1 to 100, or (of the person's own requests) a `kind` that is no kind of request; of a find, words (`q`) not written in UTF-8 or of more than 200 characters, a `limit` outside 1 to 100, or a `lang` other than `en` and `ja`; of the rows of a master and a find of them, an `on` not written `YYYY-MM-DD`

unseen.description: No such ticket, or one the person may not see. A ticket is seen by the requester's side (its requester, the one who made the request for them, and the proxies who may submit it for them that day), by the approvers' side (the approvers of its stages now and before, those who answered and the approvers they answered for, the one who sent it back, and the proxies who may approve for any of them that day), and by those the gate lets `see` it. Every operation on a ticket the person may not see answers 404, whatever the gate lets them do. An operation of one kind of request on a ticket (`/requests/<name>/tickets/{id}/…`: the request made again, an approver's edit, what the form works out on the ticket) answers 404 too for a ticket that is not of the kind `<name>`, whoever asks, as for no such ticket: what its body holds is of that kind

unoffered.description: No version of the kind is in effect now: each starts later, or an administrator stopped it, and the kind is not among the kinds of request (`list_requests`) meanwhile. The server asks the gate first whether the person may submit the kind (`submit`): to a person it does not let, it answers as for a kind there is not, saying nothing of its versions (no `from`); to a person it lets, `from` says the day the nearest later version starts, from which the request may be made, when that is decided (none when the kind is stopped and no later version is to start)

error.description: What is wrong, in a sentence for a person: the server's own, or, where the generated entry stops a value, the entry's, in the language of the list of kinds (`lang`)

from.description: The day the nearest later version of the kind starts (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the kind's day), from which the request may be made. Left out when no later version is to start, and to a person the gate does not let submit the kind

no_organization.description: No version of the organization is in effect today, or the person is not one of the people of the version in effect: the organization holds everyone's addresses, and is read by its people alone

unchosen.description: No kind of request the server holds chooses from the master

limited.description: Too many comments: the server limits how soon a person comments on a ticket again, and how many comments a ticket holds, and this one is not taken (no refusal of the machine, and the ticket is as it was). When it came too soon, `Retry-After` says in how many seconds it may be sent again, with the same idempotency key; when the ticket holds as many comments as the server takes, there is no `Retry-After`, for waiting does not change that

Retry-After.description: In how many seconds the comment may be sent again; only when it came too soon after the person's last comment on the ticket

unsigned.description: No one is signed in: the server authenticates no person for the call

oversized.description: The body is larger than the server takes

not_json.description: The body is not sent as `application/json`: the call's `Content-Type` says another type, or none

failed.description: The server failed, and says no more here (its log says how). Whether an operation that moves a ticket was done is not said: the same call is sent again with the same idempotency key, which answers what the first did if it was done
